cityQuote: What are you doing here, poet, on the ruins of St. John’s Cathedral this sunny day in spring? What are you thinking here, where the wind blowing from the Vistula scatters the red dust of the rubble?

quoteAlternatives.quote: What are you doing here, poet, on the ruins of St. John’s Cathedral this sunny day in spring?
quoteAlternatives.attribution: Czesław Miłosz, poet, opening lines of In Warsaw (1945)
quoteAlternatives.note: Short form of option 1. Written in the ruins after the Warsaw Uprising; the cathedral stands rebuilt in the Old Town.

quoteAlternatives.quote: Only the two salvaged words: Truth and justice.
quoteAlternatives.attribution: Czesław Miłosz, poet, closing lines of In Warsaw (1945)
quoteAlternatives.note: The poem’s ending; reads as a fragment out of context.
